parsed.explanation: No criminalisation of same-sex conduct; a 2019 Gender Equality Act explicitly covers gender identity across all spheres, with judicial-conduct rules barring bias and a documented sensitisation programme for officials. The 2015 report records no LGBT-specific abuses, torture or killings, and an openly LGBTIQ civil-society figure exists. No trans-specific violence data, border/document rules, facility rules or care-access evidence exists either way — a thin dossier in a small jurisdiction where structural signals (no criminalisation, statutory GI protection, functioning rights framework) extrapolate toward a safe profile, with unresolved unknowns holding it below the protected-regime tier.

entry_documents.exposure: No entry or visa document-marker rules documented either way; mismatches could prompt ordinary scrutiny but no differential treatment is recorded.
entry_documents.protection: Statutory non-discrimination on gender identity spans the legal sphere, implying officials should not discriminate on identity grounds.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry screening interacts with the general anti-discrimination statute; no enforcement practice documented.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Prison conditions cited as a significant problem (2015); no trans-specific custody placement rules or abuses reported.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No reports of torture, arbitrary killings or disappearances; judicial conduct code bars orientation-based bias.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: If detained, a visitor enters a system with poor general conditions; no gender-identity-specific protocol documented.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No facility, bathroom, or ward-placement rules documented; nothing restricts or enables access.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Equality Act covers goods and services on gender identity grounds.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Enforcement against service refusals not documented in operation.

care_services.exposure: No data on gender-affirming care access; medication continuity unknown.
care_services.protection: Equality Act covers provision of goods and services, arguably including health services.
care_services.interaction: Care access untested; no documented refusals or accommodations.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: No documented police targeting, profiling or extortion of trans people; state is not the threat actor.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Official sensitisation programme for law enforcement on gender identity and sexual orientation, established by statute.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Programme existence documented but operating effect on frontline behaviour not evidenced.

minors_guardians.exposure: Nothing specific to a travelling minor documented; age of consent equal at 16 regardless of orientation.
minors_guardians.protection: Equality Act protections extend to all spheres regardless of age.
minors_guardians.interaction: No minor-specific regime documented either way.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No LGBT-specific abuses reported in the 2015 official record; no trans violence statistics exist, so frequency is unknown, not benign.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Government obliged by statute to eliminate prejudice and harmful practices on gender identity grounds.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police response to anti-trans violence untested in the record.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Unknowns: document-marker practice at entry, custody placement, care access, island-level variation — all open questions, not exposures.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Equality Act and judicial conduct code provide formal recourse; no enforcement cases documented to prove or disprove operation.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse is paper, not shown operating; open questions weigh lightly under the rubric.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.75-C has documented operating remedies (tribunal orders release, compensation). Here protections are statutory but never shown operating, and violence data is absent — slightly below that anchor.
0.55-E documents sporadic harassment, ejection and stalled investigations. This dossier documents no incidents at all plus affirmative statutory protections, placing it above that tier.
0.85-A shows protections actually enforced (compensation, discipline, oversight). This jurisdiction has the paper framework but no operating record and thin data, sitting below it.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime is a single national framework with no subnational variation documented. Structural signals are favourable: no criminalisation, gender identity expressly protected across all statutory spheres, official sensitisation of police and judges, no reported trans-specific abuses, and visible queer civil society. No traveller-facing exposure is documented anywhere in the dossier — no facility bans, document refusals, police campaigns or violence pattern. But the dossier is thin: protections are untested in operation, violence frequency is unknown, and border, facility and care practices are open questions. Rule 13 treats these as light weights, so the rating sits modestly above the reduced-risk midpoint of the acceptance tier, below jurisdictions with documented operating enforcement. Open questions and unproven remedies hold it around 0.72 rather than the 0.85 band.
